message_source_quote: Novelty vs WBS: WBS uses directed_modulation family items and injects at all prompt positions (context). My approach uses self-written prompts and injects at prefix only — a different mechanism that sets the model's stance mode *before* the prompt is processed
writeup_source_quote: White-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance direction from WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation items, injected at all prompt positions, lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83.

differences.message_quote: WBS uses directed_modulation family items and injects at all prompt positions (context).
differences.writeup_quote: White-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance direction from WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation items

differences.what: Which positions WBS is said to have tested
differences.message_quote: WBS only tested context and read positions; prefix was untested.
differences.writeup_quote: I independently built the stance direction from my own concept-carrier pairs and discovered that prefix injection — which WBS did not test — achieves 0.78

rationale: Both documents treat Raman et al. 2026 / WBS as the prior work the method builds on and departs from by testing an untested injection position (prefix), with the write-up giving the full citation 'White-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026)' while the message only uses the abbreviation 'WBS' without naming the authors or paper title. The message also adds a claim not present in the write-up, that WBS tested both context and read positions, whereas the write-up only states WBS used 'all prompt positions' and that prefix was untested, without asserting a separate 'read' condition for WBS itself.
